I want a habit tracker app and have given you only the idea, so the first job is to settle what to build. A wrong guess about platform or stack would cost real rework. I'm starting in an empty directory, so you are free to choose the structure.

Step 1. Use the AskUserQuestion tool to interview me before writing any code. Ask only what you can't reasonably decide yourself, in one batch of at most 6 questions, each with a recommended default. Cover:
- platform (web, mobile, desktop, or CLI)
- preferred language and framework
- where data lives (local only, or an account and sync)
- which features matter for a first version (for example daily check-ins, streaks, reminders, stats views)
Proceed on your own judgment for anything smaller, such as naming, folder layout and styling. Write down those choices.

Step 2. Write the agreed scope to SPEC.md in the working directory. Keep it to one page: goal, v1 features, out-of-scope items, stack, and how to run it. Then give me a short plan and wait for my approval before you edit any other file.

Step 3. After I approve, build v1 as a small, working app. Build only what the spec lists, with no extra features, abstractions or speculative settings. Commit to git as you go if I agreed to that in step 1. Do not delete files outside this directory, and ask before any action that others would see, such as pushing or publishing.

Step 4. Verify against real behaviour. Add tests for the core logic: creating a habit, checking it off for a day, and computing streaks, including a missed day and a day boundary. Run them. Also run the app and exercise the main flow yourself. If a test or feature can't work as specified, report it instead of working around it or hardcoding results.

You're done when the tests pass, the app runs, and you have shown me the test output, the command that starts the app, and a short list of anything left out or uncertain. Give a one-line update before you start each step, and end with a brief recap.
